headline: Spotify removes 50 million AI slop and spam tracks from recommendations
summary: Spotify says it pulled roughly 50 million songs it classifies as AI-generated slop or spam from user recommendations over the past year, as part of changes favoring human artists.

claims.statement: Spotify removed about 50 million songs it considers AI-generated slop or spam from its recommendations over the past year.

sources.quote: Spotify pulled 50 million AI slop and spam tracks from its recommendations
The company said it removed 50 million such tracks from recommendations, but hasn't necessarily wiped them entirely.
On Tuesday, Spotify announced it had removed about 50m songs considered AI slop from its recommendations to users over the past year.

discrepancies.explanation: Engadget notes the removed tracks were pulled from recommendations but not necessarily deleted outright, a caveat the other two outlets' texts do not state.

quotes.quote: The company said it removed 50 million such tracks from recommendations, but hasn't necessarily wiped them entirely.

Spotify says it has removed more than 50 million songs considered AI-generated slop or spam from user recommendations over the past year. That's according to an announcement on Tuesday that says Spotify has also made changes to its recommendation system to highlight more music made by human artists.
